title: Oates Walks Out into the Blizzard
text:
Robert Falcon Scott's party of five reached the South Pole on 17 January 1912 and found that Roald Amundsen had beaten them by about a month. On the long march back, things went wrong. Edgar Evans weakened and died in February. The weather was colder than expected, fuel at the depots ran short, and the men grew weaker.

Lawrence Oates, an army cavalry officer, suffered worst. His feet were badly frostbitten and turning gangrenous, and he could barely walk. Every day he slowed the others, and he knew it. Scott wrote that Oates asked them to leave him in his sleeping bag, and that they refused.

In mid March, during a blizzard, Oates woke in the tent and, according to Scott's journal, said, "I am just going outside and may be some time." He went out and did not come back. Scott added: "We knew that poor Oates was walking to his death, but though we tried to dissuade him, we knew it was the act of a brave man and an English gentleman."

The remaining three, Scott, Edward Wilson and Henry Bowers, struggled on until another blizzard pinned them in their tent about 11 miles from a large supply depot. They died there near the end of March. A search party found the tent and Scott's journal in November 1912. Oates's body was never found; the searchers raised a cairn near where he was thought to have died.
lesson: Some team members carry burdens quietly to protect the others. Notice what people give up for the group, and never take it for granted.
people: Lawrence Oates, Robert Falcon Scott, Edward Wilson, Henry Bowers
source: Robert Falcon Scott, journal of the Terra Nova expedition (published as Scott's Last Expedition, 1913)
